title: The balance landscape
concept: Treat a hydraulic calculation as a survey of a continuous parameter field. Amber contours are constant vertical offsets from the supplied system-head relationship; a fixed mint pump curve cuts through that field. Their analytically calculated crossing is the illustrative operating point. Five compositions move from an oblique contour atlas to ruled head balance, a responsive field, a magnified evidence inspection, and a comparative operating-point trace. All relationships are illustrative and use relative axes, with no actual plant values or performed engineering claim.
metaphor: A scientific survey atlas: contours reveal the field, ruled trajectories compare head at equal flow, and a survey lens makes the remaining evidence gaps visible.
choreography: An oblique contour atlas resolves into the pump and demand crossing; finite field reveal and point acquisition.
The atlas becomes two explicit laws. Vertical ruled trajectories show head mismatch away from the crossing.
The selected resistance redraws all contour geometry while retaining the exact same pump path; higher resistance reveals the former point and a lower-flow arrow.
The operating point expands into a circular survey lens connected to unresolved units, boundaries, and OEM evidence.
Both operating points sit on one pump rail. A short trace and flow projection explain the shift before the equipment-selection boundary is stated.
interaction: The single host choice selects k = 0.7 or k = 1.5 in H_system = 0.12 + k Q². The intersection is calculated as Q = sqrt(0.88 / (0.45 + k)); no hand-positioned operating-point data. The higher-resistance choice steepens the full contour field, moves the intersection toward lower flow, and retains a dashed base relationship for comparison. The review lens uses the selected point.
contributions: Pure analytic curve and contour generators reusable for normalized scientific SVG artwork.
A directly comparable choice state with an invariant pump curve, a ghost baseline and a geometric lower-flow witness.
A magnified evidence view that distinguishes an illustrative uncertainty envelope from unresolved inputs and equipment-selection evidence.
limitations: All diagram data are illustrative; this entry performs no engineering analysis or equipment selection.
Contour offsets are a drawing convention for the supplied system-head relationship, not measured geographic or hydraulic spatial data.
The review envelope is unquantified illustrative artwork and is not a confidence interval or an assessed uncertainty bound.
The entry does not resolve units, boundaries, input provenance, pipe candidates or OEM evidence; those remain explicit human-review dependencies.
Verification is local syntax, pure rendering, identifier isolation and translation coverage; no browser rendering or target-device acceptance was performed.
